Orchestrate Your LLMs

LangChain is the "glue" that connects powerful LLMs to your real-world data and APIs. Stop just generating text—start building applications.

Launch Simulator Explain Concepts

restaurant The Kitchen Analogy

Think of a Large Language Model (like GPT-4) as a world-class Chef. They are brilliant at cooking (generating text), but they are locked in an empty room.

  • menu_book

    The Recipes (Prompts)

    The specific instructions you give the chef to get the dish you want.

  • kitchen

    The Pantry (Indexes/RAG)

    The Chef doesn't know your company's private data. LangChain stocks the pantry with your ingredients (documents).

  • soup_kitchen

    The Kitchen Staff (Chains/Agents)

    Someone needs to take the order, chop the vegetables, and serve the food. LangChain coordinates the entire workflow.

The RAG Workflow

The Building Blocks

neurology

Models (LLMs)

The reasoning engine. LangChain provides a standard interface to swap between OpenAI, Anthropic, HuggingFace, etc.

from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
model = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4")
edit_note

Prompt Templates

Dynamic recipes. Insert user variables into pre-defined instructions to guide the LLM consistently.

prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.from_template(
  "Tell me a joke about {topic}"
)
link

Chains (LCEL)

The glue. Connect components (Prompt → LLM → Output Parser) using the pipe | syntax.

chain = prompt | model | output_parser
chain.invoke({"topic": "bears"})
history

Memory

State management. LLMs are stateless; memory stores chat history and injects it into the next prompt.

history = ChatMessageHistory()
history.add_user_message("Hi!")
manage_search

Retrievers

Data fetchers. Interface to fetch documents from Vector Stores (like Pinecone/Chroma) relevant to a query.

retriever = vectorstore.as_retriever()
docs = retriever.invoke("query")
smart_toy

Agents

Autonomous actors. They use an LLM to decide which tools to use and in what order to solve a problem.

agent_executor = AgentExecutor(
  agent=agent, tools=[search, math]
)

Agents: The Loop

Unlike Chains (hardcoded sequences), Agents use a "ReAct" Loop (Reason + Act). They observe a problem, think about a tool to use, act, and observe the result.

Example: "What is 25 * 4?"

Thought: I need to calculate this. I should use the calculator.
Action: Calculator.run("25 * 4")
Observation: 100
Thought: I have the answer.
Final Answer: 100
